title: Abidjan: fake Canada job ads feeding a trafficking-run pyramid scam (INTERPOL)
summary: In February 2025 Côte d'Ivoire's national police, acting on an investigation that began in Ghana and was coordinated by INTERPOL, raided premises in Abidjan, arrested two suspects and rescued 33 victims from Benin, Burkina Faso, Ghana and Togo. The victims had answered online job advertisements promising work in Canada, contacted through numbers that appeared Canadian, and had paid nearly US$9,000 each for supposed travel arrangements. On arrival their documents were confiscated and, under threats and abuse, they were forced to recruit further victims through multi-level-marketing platforms, posing in luxury shops and hotels to keep up the illusion of success abroad. The suspects are not named and no conviction is reported.
